newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena Q1 traffic jumps but yield below par.
newsitem.headline: Sabena Q1 traffic jumps but yield below par.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena said on Friday that 1996 first-quarter traffic jumped 15 percent but that the average yield per passenger was below target.

It said in its Sabena Actueel personnel letter that the increase in traffic was one percent higher than expected. The average seat occupancy rate climbed three percentage points to 57 percent because of a lower number of seats available.

"Costs remained under control but the average yield per transported passenger remained below expectations. We will have to continue to make an effort to scrupulously meet the budgetary goals," it said in a statement.
It said the number of passengers rose more in economy class than in business class, which weighed on income per passenger.
Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, had a consolidated loss after provisions of 8.87 billion Belgian francs ($251 million) against a 1.66 billion ($47 million) loss in 1995.
The carrier is holding on to its target of reaching break-even in 1998 but must be in line with budget in June when Swissair will make an assessment of its investment in Sabena.
SAirGroup, which includes Swissair, said earlier this month it would fully write down the value -- 267 million Swiss francs -- of its Sabena stake in 1996 accounts.
